ADDITIONNAL RULES

Arianrhod 2E have compatibilies with Konosuba on multiples aspects, and somes rules can be transcribed for it. The GM decide in advance if they want to play with these rules or not if necessary, and I leave them available because Arianrhod 2E is not translated and so, difficult to play with the setting.
Pour les Règles Complète en Français, c'est ici : Konosuba TRPG Règles FR
Advanced Darkness System
By default, Darkness rules apply like normally, the advanced rules allow for various situations of Illumation
Illumination

You can use a alternative darkness system that is a little more complexe than the binary declaration of "darkness/not darkness". In cas you want to use this system, all area have a Illumination value that range from 1 to 4 :

-Illumination 1 : Total Darkness. You cannot see anything. A that illumination level, you can only target in your Engagement, and your movement is reduce to 5 meter maximum. In addition, you get -1d6 to all checks (Min. 1 dice rolled). That the default Darkness rules setting.
-Illumination 2 : Darkness at the level where moonlight or starlight is the only source of light. You get -1d6 to all checks (Min. 1 dice rolled).

-Illumination 3 : Reasonably well lit. If you are in a dungeon, this illumination let you see the present area/room, but you cannot see thing in the next area/room. You do not get penalties in movement or checks.
-Illumination 4 : Broad daylight, illuminated by the afternoon sun. You can see everything within sight without any problem.
Magic Darkness : Darkness induced by magic that cannot be reduced by ordinary tools such as the Latern; it requires magical tools such as the Magic Candle to dispel darkness of this nature.
If you are using the lighting rules, be sure to adjust stats for items and skills such as the Flashlight, Lantern and Darkvision accordingly.
Mount System
Mounted Combat

A character may ride atop a [Type: Mount] Item. A character who is riding an Item in this way is considered to be [Mounted]. Typically speaking, [Type: Mount] Items will increase your Movement as long as you are riding them. Mechanically, you do not lose the use of your hands when [Mounted], even if fictionally you are required to hold the reins with one hand – it is assumed that you let go of the reins when you require the use of your hands, then take it again once your hands are free

Mounts cannot move independently of their riders, even if they are live creatures such as horses. Also, all adventurers are assumed to have the necessary training to ride any Mounts they possess, unless stated otherwise

While in combat, mounting or dismounting (that is, gaining or cancelling the [Mounted] Status) requires a Minor Action. The GM has the right to stop players from mounting up if they are indoors or otherwise in a situation where it would be difficult to mount up. (This applies to Tandem Riders as well) In the event that it is impossible to ride a Mount in some building or location, you may treat it as if you left the mounts in the Guildhouse, or outside the dungeon.
Riding Tandem

With the rider’s permission, a character may mount up with the rider as a Passenger, gaining the [Mounted] Status as well. In combat, mounting up or dismounting as a Passenger requires that character to be in the same Engage as the main rider, and consumes a Minor Action. While riding as a Passenger, a Character may not perform any movements of their own volition ([Timing: Move Action] Skills that don’t require movement, such as the Archer’s "Foresight", may still be used.) Instead, when the main rider performs any movement, any Passengers on the mount are taken along for that movement.

However, if the effect of another Character’s Skill forces or allows the Passenger to perform a movement, that movement may be performed without restriction. If the resultant movement causes the Passenger to end up in a different Engagement from the main rider, the Passenger’s [Mounted] Status is cancelled.

Any bonuses that the [Type: Mount] Item provides applies to both the main rider and the Passenger. If the situation calls for it, the GM has the right to declare that the Passenger is unable to stay mounted. (e.g. if there is not enough space to ride tandem for some reason)

Some Mounts increase your Maximum Load; this increase affects only the Main Rider (or the owner of the Mount), and is treated as a separate Inventory. If the Mount is unusable, the Items in the Mount’s Inventory are also inaccessible
Interaction between [Off-Balance] and [Mounted]

When a [Mounted] Character who is the main rider is inflicted with the [Off-Balance] Debuff, in addition to suffering the usual penalties from the Debuff, that Character also loses the [Mounted] Status and receives 2d6 Piercing Damage. At this time, if there is a Passenger riding with that Character, the Passenger receives the same penalties as the main rider and loses the [Mounted] Status. That said, if the Passenger is the one inflicted with [Slip], only the Passenger receives the aforementioned penalties.

Furthermore, even if the [Off-Balance] Debuff is immediately cured through some means (such as the Arianrhod 2E's Monk’s <Endure> Skill or the <Nullify Bad Status> Enemy Skill), a [Mounted] Character still suffers from the 2d6 Penetrating Damage and loses their [Mounted] Status, though you do not suffer the Movement penalty that usually arises from [Off-Balance]
On the other hand, if you are immune to the [Off-Balance] Debuff, you may also ignore all further penalties arising from being afflicted with [Off-Balance] while [Mounted].
Duelling System
Duelling: That State of Combat is principally linked to the Skills of the Gladiator Class from Arianrhod 2E, here how its work.
Any Character that is an Engagement with 1 other Character and no others may use a Free Action to declare that they are [Duelling] the other Character.
Any Engagement containing a [Duelling] Character is treated as an Blocked Engagement.
Any Attacks made by a [Duelling] Character must target the declared [Duelling] target, and must be initiated from within the same Engage as the [Duelling] target.
Only Characters that have declared themselves to be [Duelling] are considered to have this Status (i.e. the target of the Duel is not considered to be [Duelling])
Cancels when... :
Another Character other than the [Duelling] target enters the Engage of the [Duelling] Character, or a [Duelling] Character expends a Free Action to cancel [Duelling].
Addition for Engagement and Movement

They exist another type of Movement, procured by skills or items that allow to "Transfer", or teleport. The Teleporation ignore all obstruction and Engagement, but the items and skills that allow to do that can have precises limitation on how or where you can Transfer.
Addition for Debuffs
Arianrhod 2E dispose de certains debuffs supplémentaires, qui ne sont pas présents dans Konosuba, principalement lié à des classes qui sont apparu au fil des extensions.
-Chained:
Some kind of curse has bound you, or you are somehow unable to move freely. You may not use Skills or Powers with [Timing: Setup Process].
Recovery: Automatically recovers at the end of the next Setup Process.
-Fear:

You are seized by fear of someone or something. -2d6 to all Checks that target the source of the [Fear]. Even if the Check targets multiple characters, as long as the [Fear] source is included among the targets, the Check suffers the -2d6 penalty.
Recovery: Automatically ends after the Main Process of the afflicted Character.
-Raging Warrior:

A state of mind where you are filled with bloodlust and single-mindedly focused on defeating the enemy within you. (n) refers to the Effectiveness Level. While under the effects of this Debuff, your Attacks get +(n)D Damage. However, any Reactions you make automatically fail, and you may not use any Skills, Cheat or Items that would normally be used as Reactions.

Optional Rules : Because It's a debuff that the Berserkers inflict ot themself and is necessary for some of their Skills. If a Skill indicate to "Choose a Debuff", like to inflict it to a enemy or similar, you cannot choose "Raging Warrior."
Recovery: Use a Minor Action to remove the Debuff, or automatically recover at the end of the Scene.
-Knockback: -Proposed change for this Debuff- The reasonning is to give more utility for the Knockback debuff that is the weakest debuff of all. The change is for the Recovery.
Lose 5 Action Points for each effectiveness level of the Knockback
Recovery: Automatically ends after the Main Process of the afflicted Character.
